items.title: Write the test runner consolidation decision document and commit it to docs/requirements/decisions/
items.context: Create docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md. Required sections: (1) Current state pinned with numbers (151 *-smoke.ts files, ~70,280 lines total, 258 test:* npm scripts (111 in root package.json + 147 in packages/main/package.json), 49 scripts/verify-*.mjs, the dist-standalone-executable pattern via `node packages/main/dist/tasks/<name>-smoke.js` consistent with testing-infra.md's general-black-box-command validation entry); (2) The three paths considered (A vitest migration, B in-house runner + manifest + c8, C B minus c8) with concrete pros/cons referencing the existing testing-infra.md project-native validation policy; (3) The chosen path (B) with explicit rationale: smokes are spawn-CLI integration scenarios not unit tests, the dist-standalone-executable pattern aligns with testing-infra.md's project-native validation policy, vitest migration would conflict with that policy, an in-house manifest+runner wraps the existing 70k lines without rewriting them and delivers CI speedup (parallel) + coverage (c8) + newcomer ergonomics (single test:all entry + selectable smokes) simultaneously; (4) The follow-up Lattice story decomposition: B1 in-house runner skeleton + manifest format + test:all entry, B2 collapse 258 test:* scripts into manifest entries (mechanical), B3 c8 coverage instrumentation + test:coverage entry, optional B4 tag/select UX improvements. Each follow-up story spec must include a one-paragraph scope sketch so future story_create calls can quote it verbatim. After: the file exists; `git log -- docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` shows a commit; `grep -c '## ' docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` >= 4 (the required sections).
items.userSees: `ls docs/requirements/decisions/test-runner-consolidation-plan.md` succeeds; opening the file shows the 4 sections (current state / paths considered / chosen path with rationale / follow-up B1-B4 stories) populated with concrete content.
